web.named_query: ("Paul S. Atkins" OR "Mark T. Uyeda") AI artificial intelligence superintelligence policy statements

summary.text: In March 2025 remarks, Uyeda said financial regulators should take a technology-neutral approach and avoid overly prescriptive rules that could become outdated or impede innovation. He also said AI has long been used in financial products and services and has enhanced trading, investing, and financial processes, while the Commission should address regulatory gaps in ways that encourage innovation and protect investors. In November 2026 remarks, he discussed machine readers of filings and said super-intelligence tools may make machine-readable data such as XBRL more valuable, while asking whether new methods might be superior. In September 2026 remarks, he noted that market participants are incorporating AI into investment decisions and operations and said the Committee’s ongoing discussion of AI’s effects on markets is helpful.

statements.text: In all seriousness, the use of artificial intelligence and other predictive data analytics in our financial markets is an important topic. Artificial intelligence and other analytic tools can process and analyze vast quantities of information efficiently, which can enhance data driven investment decisions and reduce the cost of investment advice. However, there is a potential dark side to AI as well, leading to concerns about AI’s ability to adversely affect market integrity.
